ops.title: update-block after revising 'no-op' was a grep -v short-circuit, not a daemon bug
ops.body:
Reported 2026-10-06 (plugin 0.37.4): the first `update-block` right after `revising` exited 0 and changed nothing; a second identical call applied.

Evidence (subject c5e7f44d301ea27fc2bd1eacbbe4f41d, read-only): revising.changed seq 11 at 02:28:13 PDT, the only block.upserted for fork-store is seq 12 at 02:28:38, the retry. No daemon pack rescan (which every upsert triggers via loader.Current()) was logged at 02:28:13-14, so the first update-block never reached the daemon.

Cause: the writer ran
  "$CP" revising fork-store --note ... 2>&1 | grep -v 'dropped pack' && "$CP" update-block fork-store.v2.json ... 2>&1 | grep -v 'dropped pack'
`revising` is silent on success, so `grep -v` read no lines and exited 1, and `&&` skipped update-block. Reproduced on a throwaway board with 0.37.4: the chain exits 1 and the second command never runs.

Contributing: `command -v cc-present` resolves to ~/.local/bin/cc-present, a daemonkit-cache symlink at 0.37.2, which printed "dropped pack" WARN lines on every write (the reason for the grep -v filter). 0.37.4 prints nothing on revising/update-block.

Options not taken without a ruling: (1) troubleshooting line in plugin/skills/present/reference/troubleshooting.md; (2) print confirmations (`revising: <ids>`, `upserted: <id>`, `removed: <id>`) like reply/close, which changes the documented "silent on success" contract in cli-cheatsheet.md; (3) fix the stale 0.37.2 PATH binary shadowing the plugin binary.
